text:
maya: quick heads-up — noticed a ~30% drop in prefix cache hit rate for redwood-13B-v2 on route /api/chat/complete starting ~3h ago. token-saved metric down and AcmeCorp slice looks worst.
alex: omg, saw the cost spike alert. do we have a dashboard link? :eyes:
maya: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abc123/prefix-cache-savings — look at model=redwood-13B-v2, route=chat/complete, group_by=tenant
sanjay: I pulled traces, there are more cold misses and KV cache miss latency is slightly higher too. suspecting warmup decay + a batching change from yesterday's runtime deploy.
liz: which deploy? eng-runtime pushed kernel selection tweaks yesterday afternoon (1776712345). infra-bot indicated canary passed but maybe edge-case with long prefix lengths.
perf-bot: perf-regression-detector: alert triggered for prefix_cache_hit_rate drop (p95 delta +28%). Related deploy: runtime/2026-03-17-kernel-switch. See perf_report_id=PR-3321
alex: can someone run a quick query for per-tenant key-entropy changes? I want to check if keying variance spiked for AcmeCorp.
sanjay: running now, snippet:
```
SELECT tenant, count(*) as hits, sum(tokens_saved) as saved
FROM prefix_cache_events
WHERE model='redwood-13B-v2' AND route='/api/chat/complete' AND ts > now() - interval '6 hours'
GROUP BY tenant
ORDER BY saved desc
```

sanjay: results show AcmeCorp hit_rate 0.42 -> 0.29 over window, avg prefix len ~ 48 -> 50, but entropy of top-keys increased (more unique keys)
liz: could be prompt template change on customer side too. Maya, can we check per-tenant recent prompt examples (sampled) before we escalate?
maya: sampled 1k requests for AcmeCorp — no obvious template change, mostly same prefixes but more injected session ids in system messages. looks like keying logic treated session ids as part of cache key.
alex: ah — last week we rolled stricter key normalization for system messages in kernel-select branch. it intentionally included system segments for safety. maybe we over-captured session ids.
sanjay: code pointer: runtime/prefix_keyer.go line ~210 — normalization regex changed. I can revert to previous heuristics for canary and run A/B.
liz: prefer A/B rather than full revert. spin up canary with keyer=v1 fallback policy and compare hit-rate curve.
perf-bot: perf-check: please run sampling profiler for KV hot path and batching path for the canary region.
maya: starting A/B canary: route rule => 10% traffic to keyer=v1-canary on region us-west-2. infra-bot: deploy initiated.
infra-bot: canary deployment green: runtime-canary-1767777801 -> healthy
alex: after 20m, hit_rate on canary is already 0.51 vs prod 0.31 for AcmeCorp slice. nice.
sanjay: profiler snapshot (20m window) shows increased time in cache-lookup serialization when keyer=v2 enabled — extra string concatenation + regex runs. batching heuristics also changed token-grouping threshold, causing smaller batches for mid-length prompts.
maya: so two contributing factors: keying change increased key cardinality, and batching tweak reduced batching efficiency for this prefix distribution.
liz: action items:
- revert key_normalization change (v2) for canary -> roll forward if stable (sanjay)
- adjust batching threshold temporarily to previous value for model redwood-13B-v2 (alex)
- add panel: per-tenant key-cardinality over time and example sampled keys (maya)
- add alert: sudden drop in hit_rate OR token-saved < baseline% (liz)
alex: i'll push batching config change as a runtime flag: batch.min_tokens=32 -> 24 for this model.
sanjay: reverted keyer in canary to v1, monitoring. infra-bot: deploy completed 1767777860
maya: after 10m post-revert, AcmeCorp canary hit_rate climbed to 0.55, token-saved trending back up. prod still low but plan is to rollout fix.
liz: please update dashboard docs for Debug Runbook: "Investigate prefix cache hit rate drop" with steps to check key-cardinality, recent deploys, and canary revert steps.
maya: added panel queries and sample-snippets to the dashboard. here's the panel query we used for key-cardinality:
```
SELECT tenant, approx_count_distinct(cache_key_hash) as unique_keys
FROM prefix_cache_events
WHERE ts > now() - interval '1 hour' AND model='redwood-13B-v2'
GROUP BY tenant
ORDER BY unique_keys desc
```

alex: note for longer term: we should add deterministic keyer tests in CI that fuzz session-like tokens and assert stable normalization. also add unit perf test for prefix_keyer to ensure no regression in wall-time per-key.
sanjay: filing perf task: PERF-489 add keyer microbenchmarks + add guardrail in runtime deploy pipeline (reject if per-request keyer p50 > 1ms)
liz: thanks all — final ask: add a tenant-slice widget that shows token-saved delta and hit-rate delta side-by-side so SRE/product can triage quickly.
maya: yep, on it. will also ping AcmeCorp CS with status update and mitigation note. :thumbsup:
alex: great job catching quickly. closing loop once rollout completes.
perf-bot: regression-monitor: observing hit_rate recovering in prod after batching flag tweak. continuing to monitor for 2h.
